Spec:
spec low_area_control: Field-oriented motor-control loop needing sin/cos of the rotor angle at >= 1 MSPS with max error <= 2^-10. Area is everything: minimise LUTs + FFs.
  constraint: throughput_msps >= 1
  constraint: max_abs_err <= 0.000976562
  objective: min luts_plus_ffs (HV ref 1500)
  objective: max accuracy_bits (HV ref 10)
  select: min luts_plus_ffs
  budget: 400 evals, 100/round, <= 4 rounds, eps 0.01

Evaluation budget: 400 evaluations in total, up to 100 per round,
at most 4 rounds.

Propose the first exploration plan: which families to search (1-4) and the
parameter ranges for each, with a relative budget share. Prefer families that can
plausibly meet the constraints; spend the budget where the trade-offs are. Explain
your reasoning briefly in `rationale` and per family in `why`.

families.why: Area is the sole objective and throughput only needs >=1 MSPS, which the shared-datapath iterative core meets easily (Fmax/(N+3) is still several MSPS for N<=18). Accuracy is family-independent, so for any accuracy point the iterative core is the smallest-area realisation and should own most of the Pareto front. Ranges bracket the accuracy constraint: W=10..20 spans output LSB 2^-8..2^-18 around the 2^-10 limit, N=8..18 spans the CORDIC angle-approximation floor, and the guard/rounding knobs let the search trade datapath bits for error.

Same accuracy model as iterative but k micro-rotations/cycle, so it should be area-dominated by iterative for this spec. A small share confirms whether any k=2 point sneaks onto the front (it cannot help throughput, which is already satisfied) and guards against a modelling surprise.

Registers every m stages: 1 result/cycle but N-stage datapath, so FFs scale with N and it should be area-dominated for a 1 MSPS target. Included at low share to verify it stays off the front and to catch any case where its higher Fmax changes the area/accuracy picture.

parsed.rationale: The spec is area-first: throughput >=1 MSPS is trivially met by every family (even iterative at N=18 gives several MSPS), and accuracy depends only on data_width/n_iter/angle_guard/frac_guard/rounding, not on the family. Therefore the Pareto front in (luts_plus_ffs, accuracy_bits) is almost certainly owned by the smallest-area family, iterative, and the other families are only worth probing to confirm domination. Round 1 is a broad sweep: W=10..20 straddles the 2^-10 error constraint (output LSB 2^-(W-2)), N=8..18 straddles the CORDIC angle-approximation floor, and the guard/rounding knobs expose the cheap accuracy levers. 70% of the budget goes to iterative to densely map the front near the constraint boundary and just above it (the HV reference is 1500 LUTs+FFs / 10 accuracy bits, so designs far above 1500 area or far below 10 bits are not worth many samples). The remaining 30% is split between unrolled_k and pipelined_m to test whether any non-iterative point is non-dominated; pipelined is omitted from round 1 because it is the largest-area family (N register stages) and cannot beat iterative on the only objective. Later rounds will re-allocate toward whichever family actually appears on the front and extend its ranges.
